prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Proposals include:

- EU and governance: Withdraw from the European Union and replace it with trade-based arrangements; scrap EU-derived regulations viewed as burdensome; hold binding national and local referenda on issues triggered by voter thresholds; introduce an element of proportional representation (AV+ style); create directly elected county Police, Health, and Education Boards; introduce voter-led recall of MPs; abolish regional government bodies; reaffirm parliamentary powers over treaties and war; retain devolved structures but have Westminster MPs from each nation handle devolved business part-time; consider later reform of the second chamber.

- Tax, spending, and regulation: Raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat income tax merging income tax and employee NI, with pension income below higher-rate kept at 20%; phase out employers’ NI over five years; reduce public sector size to around 1997 levels and cut quangos; replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax sharing revenue with councils; pass half of the Uniform Business Rate to local councils; abolish Inheritance Tax when feasible; restore Bank of England prudential oversight, raise bank capital ratios to at least 8%, separate retail and investment banking, and reinstate lending controls.

- Jobs and industry: Launch long-term programmes in defence procurement, nuclear power build-out, flood/coastal defences, transport upgrades, and prison construction to stimulate manufacturing and supply chains; create Production Enterprise Centres for SMEs; amend takeover rules to protect strategic firms; replace university/FE funding with student and training vouchers and convert institutions to independent charities.

- Immigration and asylum: Impose a five-year freeze on immigration for permanent settlement and aim thereafter for ≤50,000 per year under a points system; use time-limited work permits and visas; criminalize overstaying; increase border staffing; enforce removals of illegal residents; require citizenship after at least five years’ permanent residence with a test and declaration; process asylum in secure centres with first safe country rules; require visas and health insurance where no reciprocal cover exists; reinstate the Primary Purpose Rule; repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the ECHR.

- Law and order: Elected Police Boards; “life means life”; double prison capacity and end early release; strengthen home-defense rights; adopt a “three strikes” regime; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; boot camps for young offenders; abolish the Crown Prosecution Service and return prosecutions to police.

- Defence: Increase spending by ~40% (about 1% of GDP); expand the Army and Territorial Army; restore naval strength with new carriers and ships; enhance RAF lift and helicopter fleets and procure additional jets; retain and renew the nuclear deterrent; reduce MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay, conditions, and medical care; reassess the Afghanistan mission; prioritize NATO.

- Health and social care: No frontline NHS cuts; elected County Health Boards; reduce management layers; franchise services to charitable, not-for-profit, and private providers under fixed budgets; introduce opt-out Health Credit Vouchers; restore matrons and clinical leadership; expand on-the-job nurse training; review community care; restore free eye tests and dental check-ups.

- Education: School vouchers redeemable at state, private, or faith schools; strengthen literacy/numeracy; retain and expand grammar/professional schools with broader merit assessment; emphasize in-school teacher training; scrap the 50% HE participation target; restore grants via student vouchers; franchise schools under elected Education Boards; allow selection suited to academic/vocational strengths; replace Ofsted with a profession-led inspectorate; reinforce discipline; support special and home education; extend Entry to Employment programmes.

- Pensions and welfare: Create a non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week from age 65, preserving higher existing entitlements; target pension tax relief to lower/middle earners (annual cap £10,000); reinstate the 20% dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public-sector pensions; abolish PPF and NPSS. Replace multiple benefits with a flat Basic Cash Benefit (also used as student/training vouchers); allow part-time earners to keep BCB up to the personal allowance; merge child-related supports; introduce Nursery Vouchers; restrict benefits to citizens or residents of ≥5 years; require Workfare for some claimants.

- Energy and environment: Expand nuclear to up to 50% of electricity; support cleaner coal; favor offshore wind funded by markets; repeal the Climate Change Act and EU carbon schemes/directives; commission a Royal Commission on climate science; redirect spending to practical environmental improvements; promote waste reduction/recycling; incentivize electric vehicles and rail electrification; invest in flood/coastal defences.

- Transport: Invest an extra £3bn annually; improve roads and bypasses; return excess fuel duty above a set oil price; increase local say over parking/speed enforcement; charge foreign lorries via a “Britdisc”; block larger EU lorry standards; build three high-speed rail lines and reopen selected routes; lengthen rail franchises; shift freight to rail/canals; enhance port links; develop a Thames Estuary hub airport instead of expanding Heathrow, Gatwick, or Stansted.

- Housing and planning: Emphasize demand management via immigration control; bring empty homes into use; abolish regional planning bodies and the Infrastructure Planning Commission; require binding local referenda for major schemes; strengthen local plans; create elected Green Belt Conservators; scrap Section 106 levies and mandatory social housing quotas; introduce local listing; exempt listed/conservation refurbishments from the Local Sales Tax; end HIPs; allow council bond issues for social housing; end business rates on empty properties.

- Culture and civic measures: Protect key brands via a national register and takeover code changes; preserve imperial measures; support Royal Mail and Post Offices; expand teaching of national historical contributions; restrict face-coverings in certain buildings; deport violent-extremist preachers; update treason laws; ensure religious school materials align with national law; prevent parallel legal systems; create a Commonwealth Day and centre; establish an English Parliament; revise inter-nation funding formulas; make St George’s Day a holiday.

- Food, farming, and fishing: Leave the CFP, establish a 200nm EEZ, ban discards and industrial fishing, land all catches, use movable no-take zones, and strengthen protection; maintain farm supports initially, then replace with labeling and consumer promotion; support GM research with clear labeling; review and, where needed, repeal EU-origin agri rules; promote producer co-ops; back a Supermarket Ombudsman; allow county referenda on the hunting ban.

- Other: Enhance animal welfare; permit designated smoking rooms; reduce burdens on small businesses.
